body:
If you want files to be explicitly upgraded, run **Project > Tools > Upgrade Project Files**. This will update every file in the project by resaving it.

Otherwise, files are not modified until you save them again. (I'm surprised `project.godot` isn't updated to list the new version right away though, since opening a project in the editor will generally automatically save the file just after.)

I had the same behavior, opening a project created with 4.4.1 in 4.5.1, getting the warning but no changes are made. Nothing shows up in git, closing and opening the editor again still shows the project as 4.4 and warns again about the upgrade.

Doing the manual upgrade as described above works. Initially I had some errors with a plugin which were solved by updating the plugin itself, so then I tried reverting the changes to 4.4 (except for the plugin) to check if the engine fails silently when trying to upgrade the project by itself. It still didn't work without the manual upgrade (which didn't have errors anymore because I kept the updated plugin), so a possibly silent failure might not be the cause.

My system info:
Godot v4.5.1.stable - Bazzite 42.20251019.0 (Silverblue) on Wayland - Wayland display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Mobile) - integrated AMD Radeon 890M Graphics (RADV GFX1150) - AMD Ryzen AI 9 HX 370 w/ Radeon 890M (24 threads) - 30.45 GiB memory


**Update**: Playing around with the upgrade function on the same project a little more (rolling back files and doing upgrade again) doesn't update the project.godot file anymore (stuck on 4.4, but other assets are still getting updated), so the manual upgrade seems to also have issues
